subject.title: feat(feeds): search and follow signed publisher feeds

question: Should signed publisher-feed discovery, following, and persisted refresh be accepted as a core OpenClaw workflow, or should the capability remain in a plugin/ClawHub-owned surface until a narrower core seam is agreed?
rationale: The patch adds a durable remote trust boundary, user-facing CLI commands, and shared SQLite state; repository policy keeps optional integration behavior out of core when current extension seams suffice, and the available evidence does not resolve that ownership choice.

options.title: Sponsor a bounded core workflow
options.body: Accept the core CLI and state model after real runtime proof, existing-database upgrade proof, and a clean landing plan relative to the DSSE foundation PR.

options.title: Move the consumer outward
options.body: Keep only a narrowly justified generic core seam and ask for the publisher-specific workflow to ship as a ClawHub/plugin capability.

options.title: Pause pending feed-contract maturity
options.body: Wait for the producer contract and standard DSSE transition to settle before choosing a permanent consumer boundary.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a bounded core workflow
recommendation.body: Accept the core CLI and state model after real runtime proof, existing-database upgrade proof, and a clean landing plan relative to the DSSE foundation PR.

likelyOwner.reason: They hold the most direct technical context across the publisher-feed branch and its overlapping DSSE foundation, while the final product-boundary decision remains a maintainer choice.
